title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #16

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does drip irrigation do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes rain
   B. Floods the whole field
   C. Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   D. Cleans the soil

2. A cyclist pedals harder and goes faster. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Increases speed
   B. Changes shape
   C. Stops motion
   D. Decreases speed

3. Where does the digestive tube end? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Gullet
   C. Anus
   D. Stomach

4. What do vertebrates have inside their bodies that invertebrates do not? (1 mark)
   A. A shell
   B. Six legs
   C. A backbone
   D. Feathers

5. Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house? (1 mark)
   A. Windows
   B. Moonlight
   C. Sun through the door
   D. Electric bulbs

6. How many millilitres are in 2 litres? (1 mark)
   A. 20 000
   B. 20
   C. 200
   D. 2000

7. Which of these uses electricity to make heat? (1 mark)
   A. Book
   B. Electric kettle
   C. Bicycle
   D. Wooden chair

8. What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called? (1 mark)
   A. Blood
   B. Saliva
   C. Juice
   D. Faeces

9. Which wall colour helps a room to be brighter? (1 mark)
   A. Dark blue
   B. Dark black
   C. Dark brown
   D. Light colours

10. What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground? (1 mark)
   A. You fly
   B. You stop
   C. You slip
   D. You walk faster

11. Which of these is a safety rule when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Turn handles outwards
   B. Touch the hot pot
   C. Leave children alone at the cooker
   D. Turn pot handles inwards

12. Another name for the gullet is (1 mark)
   A. Oesophagus
   B. Anus
   C. Rectum
   D. Tongue

13. What direction does friction act in compared with the motion of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Opposite
   B. Sideways only
   C. Upwards only
   D. The same

14. Which of these can be made from waste for the classroom? (1 mark)
   A. A new mountain
   B. A dustbin
   C. A house
   D. A car engine

15. A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Only animals grow
   B. Trees are not plants
   C. Trees are made of stone
   D. Plants show life by growing and responding

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe. (5 marks)

17. Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life. (5 marks)

18. What is evaporation? Give one example. (2 marks)

19. Explain why a spider is not an insect. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   It gives water slowly at the roots.

2. A — Increases speed
   More force increases speed.

3. C — Anus
   Waste leaves the body through the anus.

4. C — A backbone
   A backbone is the feature that defines vertebrates.

5. D — Electric bulbs
   Bulbs are artificial light.

6. D — 2000
   2 x 1000 = 2000 ml.

7. B — Electric kettle
   A kettle is heated by electricity.

8. D — Faeces
   Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

9. D — Light colours
   Light colours reflect more light.

10. C — You slip
   Without friction you cannot grip.

11. D — Turn pot handles inwards
   Handles turned inwards cannot be knocked easily.

12. A — Oesophagus
   The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

13. A — Opposite
   Friction acts against motion.

14. B — A dustbin
   A dustbin can be made from waste materials like a bucket or box.

15. D — Plants show life by growing and responding
   Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.
